meaning: Much stronger than “annoyed.” The Greek verb pictures someone furiously angry, in a fighting mood.
facts: Used only here in the New Testament.
Built from thymos (anger, passion) and machomai (to fight), so it describes being fighting mad.
Tyre and Sidon depended on the king’s land for food, so his anger put them at real risk (v. 20).

meaning: A trusted servant in charge of the king’s bedroom.
facts: Literally “the one over the king’s bedchamber.”
Someone in that role would likely have had the king’s ear, which fits why the delegation won him over first.

meaning: Together, with one mind and one purpose.
facts: Used mostly in Acts, often for believers acting together, as in prayer.
Here it describes the Tyre and Sidon delegation coming to the king as a united group.

meaning: To feed or supply with food. Tyre and Sidon’s land got its food from the king’s territory.
facts: These were coastal trading cities with limited farmland, so they imported grain and oil.
Tyre buying food from Israel goes back centuries (1 Kings 5:11; Ezekiel 27:17).

meaning: To give a public speech to a crowd.
facts: Used only here in the New Testament.
The Jewish historian Josephus tells a parallel account of this day at Caesarea.

meaning: Struck or hit. “Smote” is just old English for “struck.”
facts: The same verb is used in Acts 12:7, where an angel strikes Peter’s side to wake him.
Same word, opposite results: one strike frees Peter, the other brings judgment on Herod.

meaning: Eaten by worms, a grisly and painful way to die.
facts: Used only here in the New Testament.
Josephus also describes Agrippa suffering severe stomach pain and dying within a few days.
In older English, “ghost” means spirit or breath, so this simply means he died.
The same verb is used for Ananias and Sapphira (Acts 5:5, 5:10), also after judgment.

meaning: Service, especially practical help. Not a church office here.
facts: Here it refers to the famine relief Barnabas and Saul brought to Jerusalem (Acts 11:29–30).
It is the root of the word “deacon.”
